blindSummary: An independent anti-trans legal-risk assessment map (July 2026 update) classifies this state/province in its mildest category — jurisdictions that largely refrain from targeting trans adults without specialising in their protection. The record carries an adverse recent fact: rather than defending its trans students and athletes, the state's seven-campus public university system affirmed compliance with new federal and state rules, plus national college-sports rules, restricting transgender women's and girls' participation in female sports, after a federal department suspended roughly $30m of its research and programme funding (March 2025) during a civil-rights investigation triggered by an executive order on trans athletes; the system's chancellor framed compliance as necessary to restore the funding.
blindSourceSummaries: an independent anti-trans legal-risk assessment map (July 2026 update): places this state/province in its mildest per-state category - jurisdictions that have 'largely refrained from targeting transgender adults' but had not taken 'extraordinary steps to protect' them - while documenting continued degradation of trans rights nationally through the 2026 legislative season.

A national broadcaster report (21 March 2025): the state's seven-campus public university system - roughly $30m in funding from the federal department concerned in fiscal 2024 - announced it 'complies' with federal and state law and national college-sports rules restricting transgender women's and girls' participation in female sports, after that department suspended its research and programme funding during a civil-rights investigation triggered by the executive order on trans athletes; the chancellor framed compliance as necessary to restore the funding.
